rationale.conceptual: The method is an established DFT elasticity calculation, but it requires understanding of convergence, strain energy expansion, and fitting. The agent must implement a strain grid (7x7x5) and quadratic fitting from paper-provided formulas, which is more than a trivial library call but not a novel algorithm.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has three main stages: geometry relaxation, a strain scan of 245 DFT single-point calculations (orchestrated), and post-processing. Managing many DFT runs, extracting energies, and fitting is non-trivial but does not involve complex multi-tool orchestration or fragile handoffs beyond standard DFT scripting.

The conceptual challenge is applying a standard DFT elasticity workflow (geometry relaxation, strain scanning, quadratic fitting) with careful settings; the paper provides necessary parameters, but translating to an open-source code and correctly implementing the strain grid and fitting makes it non-trivial. The execution involves a multi-stage pipeline with many DFT single-point calculations (strain grid), scripting, and data extraction, though it remains CPU-only and sequential.
